FitBuddy — Comprehensive Engineering & Feature Documentation

Course: SMU IS216 Web Application Development II (WAD2)
Project: FitBuddy Social Fitness & Habit Tracking Platform
Repository: github.com/elnathanshee/WAD2-FitBuddy
Production Deployment: Vercel & Neon Serverless PostgreSQL

1. Executive Summary & Architecture

FitBuddy is a full-stack, cloud-native social habit and fitness accountability platform built to meet and exceed the Singapore Management University (SMU) IS216 Web Application Development II curriculum standards.

The application integrates:

  • Reactive Frontend: Vue 3 Composition API (<script setup>), Bootstrap 5, Bootstrap Icons, Vue Router 4, Axios, and Canvas Confetti.
  • Serverless Backend: Node.js Express 5 API running as a Vercel Serverless Function (api/index.js).
  • Relational Cloud Database: Neon PostgreSQL accessed via @neondatabase/serverless connection pooling and direct SQL transactions.
  • Generative AI Coach: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (@google/genai) generating customized workout routines, SMART milestones, and automated habit imports.
  • Wearable Telemetry Simulation: Apple Health and Google Fit biometric sync recording steps, distance, active minutes, and calories into PostgreSQL check-ins.
  • Social Accountability: Dynamic weekly leaderboard rankings computed live from check-in history, peer-to-peer cheer/nudge interactions, and head-to-head friend challenges.

2. Cloud Database Schema & Security Architecture

FitBuddy leverages Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (@neondatabase/serverless) to ensure strict relational integrity, ACID compliance, and zero cold-start scaling. The database auto-initializes upon server boot via server/config/neon.js.

erDiagram USERS ||--o{ HABITS : owns USERS ||--o{ CHECK_INS : records USERS ||--o{ CHEERS : receives USERS ||--o{ CHALLENGES : participates HABITS ||--o{ CHECK_INS : tracks USERS { string id PK string email UK text password_hash string name text avatar text bio int weekly_goal int total_score timestamp created_at timestamp updated_at } HABITS { string id PK string user_id FK string name string category int target_frequency string icon string color boolean archived timestamp created_at timestamp updated_at } CHECK_INS { string id PK string habit_id FK string user_id FK string date string status text notes jsonb telemetry timestamp created_at } CHEERS { string id PK string from_user_id FK string to_user_id FK string cheer_type text message timestamp created_at } CHALLENGES { string id PK string title string challenger_id FK string opponent_id FK string target_metric numeric target_value numeric challenger_progress numeric opponent_progress string start_date string end_date string status timestamp created_at }

Password Hashing & JWT Security Design

  • Salted scrypt Hashing: Passwords are never stored in plaintext. In server/utils/auth.js, hashPassword(password) generates a cryptographically secure 16-byte random salt via crypto.randomBytes(16) and derives a 64-byte key using crypto.scryptSync(password, salt, 64).
  • HMAC-SHA256 Tokenization: Session authentication utilizes stateless JWTs signed with crypto.createHmac('sha256', JWT_SECRET) containing the user's ID, email, and a 7-day expiration timestamp (exp).
  • Route Protection Middleware: server/middleware/requireUser.js inspects the HTTP Authorization: Bearer <token> header, decodes and verifies the signature, and attaches req.user to downstream controller operations.

Feature 1: User Authentication & 1-Click Test Athlete Switcher

User Flow & Capabilities

  2. Instant Test Athlete Switcher: For grading and rapid multi-user testing, the login interface and top navigation bar feature 1-click test athlete switchers:

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (LoginPage.vue):
    <script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router'
import { authService } from '../services/authService'

const demoAthletes = ref([
  { name: 'You (Demo)', email: 'demo@fitbuddy.com', color: '#6366f1' },
  { name: 'Alex Tan', email: 'alex@fitbuddy.com', color: '#0d6efd' },
  { name: 'Bernice Lim', email: 'bernice@fitbuddy.com', color: '#198754' },
  { name: 'Charlie Wong', email: 'charlie@fitbuddy.com', color: '#ffc107' },
  { name: 'David Lee', email: 'david@fitbuddy.com', color: '#dc3545' }
])

async function quickLogin(targetEmail) {
  loading.value = true
  try {
    const res = await authService.login(targetEmail, 'password123')
    if (res.user) router.push('/dashboard')

</script>
  • Backend (server/controllers/authController.js): Queries the Neon PostgreSQL users table via sql\SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ${email}`, compares the stored scrypthash withverifyPassword()`, and issues the signed JWT.

Feature 2: Interactive Fitness & Habit Dashboard

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Overview Stat Cards: Displays Current Streak (days), Weekly Consistency Rate (%), Total Active Minutes, and Current Leaderboard Standing.
  • Dynamic Greeting Banner: Greets the logged-in user dynamically with quick navigation buttons to Habits, Leaderboard, and AI Coach.
  • Unified Telemetry Display: Integrates the Wearable Health Sync simulator, the 7-Day Consistency Matrix, and Live Friend Duels on a single responsive Bootstrap grid.

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (Dashboard.vue): Combines modular widgets (FitnessTrackerWidget.vue, ConsistencyMatrixWidget.vue, ChallengesSection.vue, and StreakCard.vue), making concurrent Axios API calls via Promise.all() to load user habits, check-ins, and challenge state.

Feature 3: Wearable Health Sync Simulator (Apple Health & Google Fit)

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Biometric Simulation: Simulates modern mobile APIs like Apple HealthKit or Google Health Connect. With one click on "Sync Apple Health" or "Sync Google Fit", real-time telemetry is calculated:
    • Daily Steps: 8,500 – 11,500 steps (with visual progress ring towards a 10,000-step goal)
    • Active Distance: Calculated dynamically based on stride length (km)
    • Active Calories: 450 – 650 kcal
    • Heart-Rate & Workout Minutes: 45 – 75 mins
  • Automated PostgreSQL Check-in: The backend locates any existing cardio or walking habit belonging to the user and automatically records an authenticated completed record in the check_ins table with rich JSONB telemetry.

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (FitnessTrackerWidget.vue): Renders live SVG progress rings and triggers POST /api/health-sync/simulate.
  • Backend (server/controllers/healthSyncController.js):
    // Generate randomized wearable telemetry
const steps = Math.floor(Math.random() * 3500) + 8000
const activeCalories = Math.floor(steps * 0.045)
const distanceKm = +(steps * 0.00078).toFixed(2)
const activeMinutes = Math.floor(steps / 130)

// Persist check-in with JSONB telemetry into Neon PostgreSQL
await sql`
  INSERT INTO check_ins (id, habit_id, user_id, date, status, notes, telemetry)
  VALUES (${checkInId}, ${targetHabit.id}, ${userId}, ${todayStr}, 'completed', 
          ${'Synced via ' + provider}, 
          ${JSON.stringify({ steps, activeCalories, distanceKm, activeMinutes, provider })})
  ON CONFLICT (habit_id, user_id, date) 
  DO UPDATE SET status = 'completed', telemetry = EXCLUDED.telemetry
`

Feature 4: 7-Day Consistency Matrix & Analytics

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Day-by-Day Performance: Visual 7-day bar chart showing daily habit completion percentages (e.g. Mon: 100%, Tue: 80%, Wed: 100%, etc.).
  • Smart Metric Interpretation: Automatically determines completion trends (Improving, Consistent, or Needs Focus) and renders motivational badges.
  • Code (ConsistencyMatrixWidget.vue): Computes day ratios using SQL aggregation over the last 7 calendar dates via server/controllers/analyticsController.js.

Feature 5: Friend Challenges & Head-to-Head Duels

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Peer Duels: Allows athletes to challenge friends to fitness duels (e.g., 50km Running Sprint or 7-Day Hydration Streak).
  • Split Progress Visualization: Real-time dual progress bars showing both the challenger's and opponent's completed metrics side-by-side.
  • Challenge Modal: Allows creating new custom challenges with customizable target metrics and end dates.
  • Code (ChallengesSection.vue): Communicates with server/controllers/challengeController.js querying the Neon challenges table.

Feature 6: Habits Tracker & Management Suite

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Category Filter Tabs: Instant client-side filtering across categories: All, Fitness (running, strength, cardio), Nutrition (water, meal prep), Mindfulness (meditation, sleep), and Recovery (stretching, foam rolling).
  • Interactive 7-Day Dot Matrix: Each habit card displays 7 interactive date bubbles representing the current week. Clicking any bubble immediately toggles completion status in Neon PostgreSQL with optimistic UI updates.
  • Habit Creation & Archival: Full CRUD capability via modal form with customizable icons, color themes, and target frequencies.

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (HabitsPage.vue & HabitCard.vue): Uses Vue 3 reactive computed properties for streak calculations and emits @toggle-day events to trigger check-in updates.
  • Backend (server/controllers/neonHabitController.js): Performs parameterized SQL queries ensuring user isolation:
    const habits = await sql`
  SELECT * FROM habits 
  WHERE user_id = ${userId} AND archived = FALSE 
  ORDER BY created_at ASC
`

Feature 7: Gemini AI Goal Coach

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Natural Language Fitness Consultation: Users select their fitness objective (e.g. Run a 10K, Build Muscle Mass, Improve Mobility, Consistent Hydration) and input their current fitness level.
  • Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Reasoning: The server passes the user's objective, experience level, and existing habit history to Gemini 2.5 Flash via @google/genai.
  • Structured JSON Output: The model responds with:
    1. A motivational SMART training plan with weekly progression advice.
    2. Recommended atomic habits (name, category, frequency, suggested icon, and color).
  • 1-Click Habit Import: Users can click "Add to My Habits" directly within the AI recommendation card to instantly create the habit in their Neon database without leaving the modal.

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (AiGoalCoachModal.vue): Interactive Bootstrap modal rendering structured Gemini recommendations, loading spinners, and import handlers.
  • Backend (server/controllers/aiController.js):
    import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai'

const ai = new GoogleGenAI()

export async function getAiGoalAdvice(req, res) {
  const { goal, experienceLevel, existingHabits } = req.body
  const prompt = `You are FitBuddy's elite athletic coach.
The athlete wants to achieve: "${goal}".
Current experience level: "${experienceLevel}".
Their current habits: ${JSON.stringify(existingHabits || [])}.

Return strict JSON format:
{
  "coachAdvice": "Detailed strategic advice and progression roadmap",
  "recommendedHabits": [
    {
      "name": "Habit Name",
      "category": "Fitness" | "Nutrition" | "Mindfulness" | "Recovery",
      "targetFrequency": 3 to 7,
      "icon": "bi-activity",
      "color": "#0d6efd",
      "reason": "Why this habit helps"
    }
  ]
}`

  const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
    model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',
    contents: prompt,
    config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' }
  })

  const parsed = JSON.parse(response.text)
  res.json(parsed)
}

Feature 8: Weekly Social Leaderboard & Cheer Engine

User Flow & Capabilities

  • Dynamic Weekly Rankings: Leaderboard rankings are computed live from check-ins recorded over the current 7-day rolling window: $$\text{Score} = (\text{Check-ins Completed} \times 10) + (\text{Active Streak Bonus} \times 5)$$
  • Podium Visualizations: The top 3 ranked athletes are highlighted with Gold, Silver, and Bronze podium cards, custom avatars, and trophy badges.
  • Social Cheer & Nudge System:
    • Clicking "Cheer" fires a burst of festive confetti across the screen using canvas-confetti and logs an entry in the Neon cheers table.
    • Clicking "Nudge" sends an encouraging nudge notification to an athlete whose streak may be slipping.
  • Activity Inbox: Displays the latest cheers received by the logged-in user with timestamps and cheering user details.

Code Implementation

  • Frontend (Leaderboard.vue):
    import confetti from 'canvas-confetti'

async function sendCheer(athlete) {
  try {
    await api.post('/api/leaderboard/cheer', {
      toUserId: athlete.id,
      cheerType: 'fire',
      message: 'Keep crushing it! 🔥'
    })
    confetti({
      particleCount: 80,
      spread: 60,
      origin: { y: 0.7 }
    })
    athlete.cheerCount = (athlete.cheerCount || 0) + 1
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Failed to send cheer:', err)
  }
}
  • Backend (server/controllers/neonLeaderboardController.js): Executes an aggregated PostgreSQL query joining users and check_ins within the current week:
    const athletes = await sql`
  SELECT 
    u.id, u.name, u.email, u.avatar, u.bio,
    COUNT(c.id) AS weekly_completed_count,
    COUNT(ch.id) AS cheer_count
  FROM users u
  LEFT JOIN check_ins c ON c.user_id = u.id AND c.status = 'completed' AND c.date >= ${weekStartStr}
  LEFT JOIN cheers ch ON ch.to_user_id = u.id
  GROUP BY u.id, u.name, u.email, u.avatar, u.bio
  ORDER BY weekly_completed_count DESC, u.name ASC
`

4. Deployment Architecture & Build Pipeline

The project features a dual-root Vercel architecture designed to build and run seamlessly regardless of whether the Vercel project's Root Directory is set to ./ (repository root) or FitBuddy (frontend folder).

Automated Build Pipeline (scripts/build.js)

When Vercel triggers a build:

  1. scripts/build.js inspects process.cwd().
  2. If running from repository root, it executes npm install --prefix FitBuddy --include=dev to ensure vite and Vue compilation plugins are present.
  3. It compiles the Vue 3 app (npm --prefix FitBuddy run build), generating production assets into FitBuddy/dist.
  4. It mirrors the compiled bundle to ./dist so Vercel's default output directory detector locates it immediately.
  5. It ensures backend server files in server/ are mirrored into FitBuddy/server/ and serverless entrypoint api/index.js is duplicated to FitBuddy/api/index.js.

Environment Variables Configuration

To run in production or locally, the following environment variables are configured in Vercel and .env.local:

Variable Name Description Example / Source
DATABASE_URL Neon PostgreSQL pooled connection string postgresql://neondb_owner:***@ep-***-pooler.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require
GEMINI_API_KEY Google AI Studio API Key for Gemini 2.5 Flash AIzaSy...
JWT_SECRET Secret key used to sign and verify HMAC-SHA256 JWTs fitbuddy_secret_production_key_2026
PORT Local Express development port 3000 (or 3899 for screenshot runner)
NODE_ENV Environment identifier production
